newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Army to be deployed as flood threat worsens.
newsitem.headline: Canada Army to be deployed as flood threat worsens.

text.p: About one hundred Canadian Armed Forces soldiers will start sandbagging towns in Southern Manitoba this weekend after officials revised their flood outlook for the region on Friday.

Manitoba government officials said on Friday flooding along the Red River is expected to be at least two feet higher than the worst of this century and 800 square miles of farmland may be under water.
Officials had previously forecasted that 400 square miles of farmland may be flooded.
"In 1979, 400 square miles were flooded and we may be looking at significantly greater than that, perhaps double," Manitoba Natural Resources director Larry Whitney told reporters on Friday.
"Anything above 1979 will be the flood of the century and it looks like we'll be above 1979 at best estimate, for sure," Whitney said.
Officials said about one hundred Canadian Armed Forces personnel will begin sandbagging operations on Saturday.
"As circumstances dictate, that request for assistance may expand," said Manitoba Emergency Management Organization executive coordinator Harold Clayton.
The revised Manitoba flood outlook was due to a higher- -than-expected Red River flood level in Grand Forks, North Dakota and higher flows from tributaries.
The Red River is forecast to crest at the Canada-U.S. border on April 24 and at Winnipeg on April 29, Manitoba Natural Resources said.
"The dikes have been raised in some places up to two feet to provide extra protection against wave action from this large lake that will form," Whitney said.
Seeding of spring wheat, barley, durum, canola and flax usually begins on May 7. But last year's crest on April 20 delayed Red River seeding to May 29, Manitoba and private crop reports said.
